sections.overview: Protochromys fellowsi is a murid rodent endemic to the mountains of Papua New Guinea and the only known species in its genus.
sections.identification: It is medium-sized, long-tailed and has dense, soft fur; its pale incisors and skull traits help distinguish its genus from related mosaic-tailed rats.
sections.habitat: Records come from high montane forests of Papua New Guinea’s Central Cordillera, at roughly two and a half kilometres elevation.
sections.diet: Examination of preserved specimens found mushroom material in the stomachs, evidence that fungi are an important food; the small sample does not define its full diet.
sections.behavior: Few localities are documented; this may partly reflect difficulty detecting it.
sections.reproduction: No reproductive observations are reported here.
sections.ecology: The species was originally described in Melomys but is now placed in its own genus, Protochromys; this taxonomic change reflects distinctive anatomical traits.
sections.conservation: The Mammal Diversity Database reports a Least Concern IUCN assessment; the limited field records still leave aspects of its ecology poorly known.

sources.title: Systematic reviews of New Guinea Coccymys and ‘Melomys’ albidens — American Museum of Natural History Bulletin
